chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is the borrowed item (for use) liable for loss?' He said, 'All that you borrow is liable for loss, but your liability for its loss is not required except for gold and silver, for they are liable. Unless it is stipulated that whenever it is lost, you are not liable for its loss. And likewise, all that you borrow and it is stipulated upon you is liable for you. And gold and silver are liable for you even if it is not stipulated upon you.'

key_terms.يَلْزَمُكَ تَوَاهُ: You are liable for its loss

ai.seo_question: What is the borrower's liability for loss when borrowing items for use versus gold and silver in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *'ariyyah* (gratuitous loan for use) and *qard* (loan for consumption) by establishing that gold and silver, being consumable valuables, incur inherent liability for loss unless explicitly exempted. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that precious metals are treated differently from non-consumable tools, emphasizing the importance of contractual stipulations (*shart*) in defining borrower responsibility. It serves as a foundational text for understanding property rights and risk allocation in Islamic commercial law.
